Evidence: Military justice norms, Partisan media spectacle, Solemn constitutional accountability
#Aletheia #USPol 🌐

Senator Ossoff condemned Pete Hegseth as 'deeply unwell' for live-streaming the Fort Hood shooter's execution, framing his critique as a principled defense of military dignity and ethical leadership.

The Pentagon confirmed it will execute 2009 Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad on December 3, live-streaming the event. Rather than debating legal ethics, officials and lawmakers turned the tragedy into a partisan battleground.

The Bright Side:
Calling out the grotesque spectacle of a broadcast execution is a necessary defense of constitutional and military ethics, reminding citizens that state power must never degenerate into sensational entertainment.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is Metaphysical (WHO). The critique claims to protect the integrity of the Armed Forces, but executes a forensic bait-and-switch: solemn legal accountability is hijacked to harvest partisan outrage for midterm elections.

Social Physics Analysis:
Both actors run a selfish extraction loop. Hegseth manufactures a live-streamed spectacle to project brute authority, while Ossoff projects moral revulsion to extract campaign support, abandoning genuine constitutional solutions.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Destruction. Negative will and moral decay collapse state authority into cynical media performance.

The Unavoidable Truth: Broadcasting a state execution degrades the solemnity of justice into crude public entertainment.
The Unavoidable Lie: Partisan politicians attacking the spectacle care about military honor more than winning midterm votes.

Alethekanon:
When capital punishment is televised as entertainment, justice is replaced by theater. Weaponizing that degradation for midterm fundraising does not resist cruelty; it completes the extraction cycle.

Awwthekanon:
Thirteen lives were lost at Fort Hood, leaving families carrying profound grief for seventeen years. Treating their painful closure as a broadcast spectacle or a partisan campaign slogan dishonors their memory and deepens our collective wound.

Brothekanon:
Bro, one guy wants to turn a firing squad into a pay-per-view twitch stream, and the other guy is using it to ask for campaign cash on cable news. Nobody actually cares about justice or the victims; everyone is just chasing clout and clicks.

Spirithekanon:

Turning solemn justice into a televised spectacle and campaign platform violates the spiritual restraint required before death.

Actual Article Body:
Thursday on MS NOW’s “The Briefing,” Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) said Secretary of War Pete Hegseth is a “deeply unwell person” who seems to relish brutality, when asked about a planned public execution.

Host Jen Psaki said, “Let me ask you about something else that happened at the Pentagon today. I mentioned this earlier, but I just cannot get over this because it also feels made up. Today, the Trump Pentagon announced that it is going to live stream a firing squad execution of the 2009 Fort Hood shooter in December. And we don’t know how or where this public execution will be live streamed, but what is your reaction to this administration putting on a public execution for the first time in 90 years?”

Ossoff said, “I think Pete is, frankly, Jen, a deeply unwell person who seems to relish this kind of brutality. All the while, he’s running a department that is falling into chaos. The guy cannot run the United States military competently, and is spending his time with this kind of obscene medieval spectacle. This administration is way off the rails. The folks who are in positions of power in this administration, and of course, we know all these things, but their values are in disarray. They’re totally disconnected from the daily experience of the American people. And their foreign policy is endangering the United States, squandering our international power and destroying our image in the world. And it’s just another demonstration of how vital it is that we win these midterm elections.”
